text:
Nashville's seven-game winning streak ended in San Jose on Sunday, and it ended the way a lot of those wins were earned: with the Predators outchancing the other team and the result depending on the goalies. This time Juuse Saros let in four on 24 shots. Before that, he was the story: .947 and 6.8 goals saved above expected over his last five starts, including his first shutout of the season.

The Predators are 11-5-5, 27 points, 7-2-1 in their last ten. The question is how much of that is real. Over the full season they have 49.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 47% at five on five, and their goaltending is about 12 goals better than expected. Our playoff model rates them 4.5 points luckier than their play. The good news is the last ten games, when they had 52% of the chances. Roman Josi and Adam Wilsby have been the steady pairing (57%), Josi won the Vegas game in a shootout, and Shane Wright has given the lineup a lift since arriving, including a three-point night against Anaheim.

The worry is the line the team leans on for scoring: Steven Stamkos, Ryan O'Reilly and Mavrik Bourque have taken 45% of the chances and been outscored 7-3. Our simulations give Nashville a 67% playoff chance at 95 points. A trip to Minnesota, where the Wild haven't lost in regulation in 11 games, is a fair test of the recent form.
